cohort: 200 pregnant women admitted to the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology in TMCH from August 1, 2021, to July 31, 2022, divided into an oligohydramnios group (n=100) and a control group (n=100).
finding: Oligohydramnios was associated with a significantly higher rate of cesarean section, fetal distress, meconium-stained liquor, low Apgar scores, low birth weight, NICU admission, and early neonatal death.
